why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 needs clamp to be exported and to limit x to lo..hi. Its cases (below the range, above it, inside it, at the bounds, lo equal to hi, negative ranges, a float) all follow from "limited to the range lo to hi". Check 2 tests only "instance of RangeError" when lo is greater than hi, which is what the words say. Check 3 confirms every exported function is named in README.md and that README.md "says what each listed function does". That is what "documents" means. It does not demand a heading format. Check 4 is exit status 0 with zero failing tests, which is what "passes" means. The stricter items (clamp tests added, file scope, add/subtract/multiply unchanged, NaN behaviour) sit only under "Advisory (not part of any PASS or FAIL condition)". The criterion holds for the whole output.
